newsitem.title: USA: Clinton confers with Spanish prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Clinton confers with Spanish prime minister.

text.p: President Bill Clinton met at the White House on Wednesday with Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and discussed the country's role in NATO.
"We want Spain integrated fully into the NATO command structure," Clinton said at the start of the talks.
Spain joined the NATO alliance in 1986 but is not yet part of its integrated military structure. The Spanish government has indicted that it planned to fully join the alliance later this year.

The focus of Aznar's meetings in Washington was on NATO and the alliance's expansion. Madrid will host a landmark summit in July that was expected to open the alliance to Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic -- former members of the Warsaw Pact.

The two leaders also discussed the situation in Cuba, a former Spanish colony. Aznar's centre-right government has won praise from U.S. officials for its hard line against Cuban President Fidel Castro's Communist government.
"We feel Spain has been working hard ... on Cuba and has been a voice for changing Cuba, and we really appreciate that policy," an administration official said after the talks.
